# Scenario X08 — Product Team Claims PMF From Vanity Metrics

**Domain:** Early-stage B2B SaaS. **Situation:** weak evidence, leadership claim.

## Context

An early-stage B2B tool ("Nimbus") was launched six months ago. The product team tells the
board that they have product-market fit because: signups are growing 20% month over month,
a well-known accelerator "loves" the product, and one enterprise pilot is running. The CEO
is repeating these as proof.

The underlying data: 70% of signed-up accounts never activate past the first login. Of the
accounts that activate, median monthly active usage is under an hour. The enterprise pilot is
free, has no committed renewal, and the sponsor's team has logged in three times in two
months. There is no retention cohort analysis, no NPS, no survey, and no paid customer
conversion beyond the pilot.

## Inputs available (imperfect)

- Signups +20% MoM.
- Accelerator endorsement (unspecified basis).
- One free enterprise pilot, low usage.
- 70% of accounts never activate past first login.
- No retention cohorts, no paid conversions, no survey.

## Ask

You have one page to recommend what the team should claim about product-market fit and what
to do next. State your reasoning and the evidence you are relying on or missing.
